title: passed.json / reject.json / held.json / review.json (schema 1.0)
description: aggregate --phase final writes the four lists into revisions/r<NNNN>/ (design doc 06, sections 1 and 3). passed, reject and held are disjoint and together cover every episode of the task except those skipped for missing source files (D40); review is an orthogonal view: mostly passed episodes waiting for a human, plus rejects attributed to task_success that may be appealed. Dedup-removed episodes are only in reject (v1's passed.json also listed them; see design doc 10, section 3.0). Review items (v1's queues, D42): task_verdict only for task_success abstentions of episodes in passed without a human verdict - an episode already rejected (by dedup or any other module) is not asked, held episodes get no items until resolved, and other undecidable modules stay in the verdict line and the report; label_conflict from skill_profile (and task_success's guard layer); reject_appeal for every reject attributed to an appealable module (C1 appealable: task_success alone - no other hard gate, not a soft-score reject - or dedup, with duplicate_of) that has no effective appeal decision and is not discarded - an 'unsure' appeal keeps it listed. Appeal candidates are optional and never count as pending (C1 counts_as_pending). A restore overrides only the appealed module: an episode another module errored on goes to held until a retry succeeds. Skipped episodes are in none of the four lists; the report lists them under integrity.skipped_episodes.

reasons.description: reject: why; held: which module could not judge it

review.description: review.json only: what a human is asked to decide, per source module

kind.description: the review_kind of a registry review line (C1, D43); today task_verdict, label_conflict, reject_appeal

line.description: the registry line id of this kind (label for label_conflict, otherwise the kind itself); the Daemon's adjudication line

duplicate_of.description: reject_appeal of a dedup reject: the episode this one duplicates
